What changed: Home and away goal factors from 2025-26 (1.53 vs 1.22 goals per match: HomeAdv 1.113, AwayAdv 0.887).
How it was tested: 2025-26 preseason run, all 380 matches, out-of-sample RPS.

What changed: Mix pre-season and current ratings by games played: (pre x k + current x games) / (k + games).
How it was tested: 2025-26 backtest: 10 runs (preseason, after GW3 ... GW34), 1,790 out-of-sample predictions; k = 5, 10, 15.
Result: blend_15 RPS 0.2156 vs 0.2321 without blending (-7.1%); early season -11.7%, after GW3 -17%. No blending only slightly better from GW26.
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED k = 15 in Excel (Settings B16, Team Strength updated D:E). SQL adopted variant stays home_adv (exported ratings already blended). See Blend test sheet.

What changed: Promoted clubs rated by regression on Championship ratings (39 clubs) WITHOUT the usual 25% reversion.
How it was tested: 2025-26 and 2026-27 preseason runs; matches involving promoted clubs.
Result: Worse in both seasons: 2025-26 0.2164 vs 0.2091 (+3.5%); 2026-27 0.2458 vs 0.2365 (+3.9%, 15 matches). Championship form explains ~7% of Premier League form (r = 0.27).
Decision / where it lives: NOT ADOPTED. Kept regression + 25% reversion (current method). Regression shown in model Settings B23:B27 and on Data_promoted. Re-check 2026-27 at season end.

What changed: 2025-26 after GW22 run held end-of-season ratings and simulations.
How it was tested: Rebuilt from results up to GW22 only; checked with SQL ratings query.
Result: GW22 RPS changed from 0.2035 (leaked) to 0.2176 (honest).
Decision / where it lives: Fixed 8 Oct 2026 (ratings_GW22_fixed.csv, sims_GW22_fixed.csv).

What changed: Historical Championship Data used the wrong Premier League goal totals for 2023-24 promoted clubs (1091, should be 1115) and Sunderland 2024-25 (1091, should be 1045). 2026-27 estimates removed from the regression.
How it was tested: Totals checked against the final tables.
Result: Regression attack slope 0.224 -> 0.214; conclusions unchanged.
Decision / where it lives: Fixed 9 Oct 2026 in the model and in SQL promoted_history.

What changed: Average bookmaker odds (football-data.co.uk) turned into probabilities with the margin removed; scored on the same matches.
How it was tested: All 2025-26 runs (2,170 predictions) and 2026-27 preseason (50).
Result: Bookmakers RPS 0.2056 vs blend_15 0.2159 (5% behind) and home_adv 0.2294 (12% behind). Late season 0.2093 vs 0.2053. Ahead after GW34 and in 2026-27 preseason (small samples).
Decision / where it lives: Benchmark only; nothing adopted. Re-download odds every few weeks (Step 4.6).

What changed: Understat xG runs above actual goals (2025-26: 1,162 xG vs 1,045 goals, +11%; 2026-27: +16%).
How it was tested: League totals compared in Data_team_xg; 2026-27 also compared with a second provider (+7%).
Result: Raw charts showed almost every team scoring and conceding below xG.
Decision / where it lives: Luck charts use league-adjusted columns J:K. Ratings unaffected (relative to league average). Understat kept for both seasons.

What changed: Current-season ratings mixed with xG ratings (team xG per game / league xG per game, 25% reversion): final = (1 - w) x blended rating + w x xG rating. Match xG from Understat.
How it was tested: 2025-26 runs after GW3 to GW34 (9 runs, 1,790 out-of-sample predictions); w = 0.5 (xg_50) and 1.0 (xg_100), both on top of blend_15.
Result: xg_50 RPS 0.2120 vs blend_15 0.2156 (-1.7%), better in all 9 runs; xg_100 0.2125. Gap to bookmakers (0.2057) cut from 4.8% to 3.1%. Pre-season runs unchanged.
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED w = 0.5 in Excel (Settings B31:B35, Team Strength updated H:L; Attack/Defence now J:K). SQL adopted variant stays home_adv. Weekly: refresh xG, export A, J, K.

What changed: Second model fitted in Python (dc_model.py): all teams' attack/defence fitted together, home advantage, low-score correction (rho), time decay (XI 0.0019) and shrinkage (RIDGE 10). Predictions stored as source dixon_coles.
How it was tested: 2025-26 runs after GW5 to GW34 (8 runs, 1,440 predictions; preseason and GW3 skipped: under 50 matches of history) and 2026-27 preseason (50). RIDGE 3/5/10/20 tried.
Result: dixon_coles RPS 0.2166 vs xg_50 0.2117 and blend_15 0.2152 on the same 1,440 matches. 2026-27 preseason: 0.2031 vs 0.2038 (small sample). RIDGE 10 best.
Decision / where it lives: NOT ADOPTED as main model (xg_50 stays). Kept as a second opinion: Model vs Dixon-Coles sheet. Re-test at the end of 2026-27, when it has a full season of history. Weekly: set ONLY_RUN, run python dc_model.py.

What changed: Loaded the 2023-24 and 2024-25 results, odds, xG and the 2023-24 final table. Built the 2024-25 backtest runs (preseason through after GW34). Dixon-Coles now also learns from up to 2 previous seasons.
How it was tested: every model was re-scored out-of-sample on 2024-25 and compared with 2025-26. Dixon-Coles 2025-26 was re-fitted with the extra history.
Result: Over both seasons xg_50 scored best with an RPS of 0.2112 (0.2104 in 2024-25 and 0.2119 in 2025-26). Dixon-Coles was close behind at 0.2125 (0.2131 and 0.2120); its 2025-26 score improved from 0.2166 once it could use previous seasons. blend_15 scored 0.2127 (0.2098 and 0.2156), so it was slightly better than xg_50 in 2024-25 but worse in 2025-26. home_adv was clearly worst at 0.2253 (0.2185 and 0.2320).
Decision / where it lives:
Blending is confirmed.
The xG gain is smaller in 2024-25, but xg_50 is still best over both seasons, so it stays the main model.
Dixon-Coles is now close behind and stays as the second opinion.

What changed: New SQL views score every run’s season forecasts against the final table: title, top-4 and relegation chances (Brier score), predicted finish (places out) and the full spread of finishing positions (position RPS). Empty tables dyn_sim_summary and dyn_position_probs created for Upgrade 11.
How it was tested: The Excel model’s 10 runs for 2025-26 were scored against the final table and compared with the Dixon-Coles season simulations on the same 10 runs. A calibration table checked the 200 top-4 forecasts in 20% bands.
Result: Excel model 2025-26 (10 runs): title / top-4 / relegation Brier 0.0167 / 0.0999 / 0.0494, position RPS 0.1111, 2.78 places out (3.94 pre-season to 1.15 after GW34). Dixon-Coles better on the same runs: 0.0163 / 0.0914 / 0.0350, 2.51 places out. Top-4 calls overconfident at the extremes (80-99% forecasts happened 77.8% of the time).
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED as a standard check; no model change. Dixon-Coles stays as second opinion. Overconfidence tested in Upgrade 11. Views v_season_scores and v_position_rps (script 24); chart on Data_season_scores. Re-score 2026-27 at season end.

What changed: Match probabilities averaged from the main model and Dixon-Coles: 75/25 (ens_dc_25) and 50/50 (ens_dc_50). New view v_main_predictions holds the main model’s predictions for every run.
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26 runs after GW3 to GW34 that Dixon-Coles fitted (3,585 out-of-sample predictions). Rule: adopt only if it beats xg_50 in both seasons.
Result: ens_dc_25 RPS 0.2108 vs xg_50 0.2112, better in both seasons (0.2102 vs 0.2104 and 0.2113 vs 0.2119). ens_dc_50 also 0.2108 but worse than xg_50 in 2024-25. Before Upgrade 7’s extra history the ensembles did not help.
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED ens_dc_25 for match predictions (small but consistent gain). Excel model and season simulations unchanged. Stored in external_predictions; run block 9.3 after dc_model.py each week. Shown on Model comparison.

What changed: Python script (market_model.py) fits attack/defence ratings that reproduce the bookmakers’ margin-free odds for matches already played (source market). Ensembles: ens_mkt_50 (main model + market) and ens_3way (main model, market and Dixon-Coles). Decay tuned: odds count half after about 10 weeks (XI 0.01), ridge 2.
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26 runs after GW3 to GW34 (3,585 out-of-sample predictions). Four decay/ridge settings tested; best kept. Rule: adopt only if better than ens_dc_25 in both seasons.
Result: Tuning improved market from 0.2135 to 0.2129. ens_mkt_50 and ens_3way 0.2111: best in 2025-26 (0.2108 vs 0.2113) but worse in 2024-25 (0.2114 vs 0.2102). ens_dc_25 stays best at 0.2108. Bookmakers 0.2008 / 0.2057.
Decision / where it lives: NOT ADOPTED; ens_dc_25 stays. Past odds alone do not capture the bookmakers’ edge (team news, transfers). Market predictions kept in external_predictions as a benchmark. Re-test at the end of 2026-27.

What changed: Python script (dynamic_sims.py) simulates the rest of each season 10,000 times from the main model’s ratings, with each team’s attack and defence varied at random by a set amount (shrinking as the season goes on). Tested at 0%, 5%, 10% and 15%. Results stored in dyn_sim_summary and dyn_position_probs.
How it was tested: All 2024-25 and 2025-26 runs (10 per season) scored against the final tables with Upgrade 8’s measures, and compared with the old Excel sims and Dixon-Coles on the same 2025-26 runs. Top-4 calibration checked across 400 forecasts.
Result: Position RPS 2024-25: all settings 0.066 (no difference); 2025-26: 0.0952 (0%) to 0.0941 (10%) and 0.0931 (15%). dyn_10 beat Dixon-Coles on 2025-26 (top-4 0.0905 vs 0.0914, relegation 0.0277 vs 0.0350). Even with no uncertainty, the rebuilt model beat the old Excel sims (relegation 0.0269 vs 0.0494); the Upgrade 8 overconfidence came from the old sims (80–99% forecasts now happen 91% of the time, was 78%).
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED 10% uncertainty (dyn_10) for season forecasts: neutral in 2024-25, better in 2025-26; 15% rejected as it hurt top-4 and relegation in 2024-25. Weekly: set ONLY_RUN and run python dynamic_sims.py. Shown on Season forecast (uncertainty) sheet.

What changed: Two published methods added as yardsticks (benchmarks.py): pi-ratings (Constantinou & Fenton 2013: home/away ratings updated by goal margin) and Dixon-Coles fitted on expected goals (dc_xg). Then ensembles of the main model with dc_xg (25% and 50%).
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26 runs after GW3 to GW34 (3,585 out-of-sample predictions), every model on the same matches, plus a comparison with the bookmakers. Rule: adopt only if better than ens_dc_25 in both seasons.
Result: ens_dc_25 beat both benchmarks (0.2108 vs dc_xg 0.2111 and pi_ratings 0.2191). ens_dcxg_50 was best of all: 0.2097 / 0.2111 (both 0.2104), better than ens_dc_25 in both seasons. 7.4% better than the original model (base 0.2271). Gap to bookmakers 4.4% (2024-25) and 2.6% (2025-26).
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED ens_dcxg_50 as the main match model (replaces ens_dc_25; small but consistent gain). Weekly: run benchmarks.py with ONLY_RUN, then block 12.5. Re-check at season end. Dixon-Coles kept as second opinion.

What changed: Transfermarkt squad values (1 August each season, 80 clubs over 4 seasons) turned into attack/defence ratings by regression on earlier seasons only. Tested as a pre-season mix for all clubs (15–50%) and for promoted clubs only (50%, 100%).
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26 runs, all stages. Rule: adopt only if better than xg_50 in both seasons, then re-checked inside the main ensemble.
Result: All-club mixes helped 2025-26 but hurt 2024-25 at every weight. Promoted clubs only at 50% (value_prom_50) beat xg_50 in both seasons (0.2095 / 0.2125 vs 0.2096 / 0.2128); inside the main ensemble 0.2096 / 0.2110 vs 0.2097 / 0.2111.
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED for promoted clubs only: pre-season rating = 50% usual rating + 50% squad-value rating (small but consistent gain). The main model ens_dcxg_50 now builds on value_prom_50. 2026-27: Coventry, Hull and Ipswich updated in the model workbook (Squad values sheet, ValueWeight 0.5). Re-test at season end.

What changed: Fantasy Premier League API (free) gives injuries, suspensions and doubts each week. For each team, the share of its 14 regulars’ quality unavailable (weighted by minutes and price) adjusts next gameweek’s attack and defence (BETA 0.3). Manual adjustments log in the model’s Availability sheet; switch with Settings UseAvail.
How it was tested: Can only be tested going forward (past injury lists aren’t available). Each run’s next-gameweek matches scored with and without the factors (v_availability_test).
Result: Started 2026-27 after GW6 (e.g. Bournemouth attack ×0.926 for GW7). Verdict after 8–10 runs.
Decision / where it lives: IN TEST: switched on in the sims (UseAvail = Yes). Decide at about GW18 with block 14.7; switch off (No) if it doesn’t help.

What changed: Added per-match player stats (FPL-Core-Insights), team stats and referees (football-data.co.uk) and Understat 2023-24 player xG to prem_sims, with views linking them to my team and match ids (script 29, blocks 15.1a-k). Why: Player and team markets need player-level and team-level history, not just results. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Row counts per season from each source, match linking to my matches table, and cross-checks between the two sources (blocks 15.1c-h).
Result: 380 matches per past season from each source; every match from 2023-24 linked; the two sources agree on goals and cards; 90%+ of Understat minutes matched to FPL players.
Decision / where it lives: Kept

What changed: player_minutes.py predicts each player's chance to start, come on, and his minutes, from recent line-ups and the official FPL availability flags. Why: Every player market depends on whether and how long he plays. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Out-of-sample on 2024-25 and 2025-26: predicted start chance and minutes before each gameweek vs what happened, against a last-5-games baseline (blocks 15.2c-e).
Result: Start chances calibrated. Fixed 16 Oct 2026: doubtful players' start chance can no longer be scaled back up to make 11 starters.

What changed: player_rates.py estimates each player's goals, xG, xA, shots, shots on target, fouls, fouled, tackles and cards per 90, shrunk towards his position's average. Why: Rates times expected minutes give each player's expected count in the next match. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Out-of-sample chance of 1+ in the next match, model vs baseline, both seasons (blocks 15.3b-c).
Result: Beat the baseline in both seasons.
Decision / where it lives: Kept

Upgrade: 15.4 Team counts (corners, fouls, cards, shots, tackles)
What changed: team_counts.py predicts each team's corners, fouls, yellows, reds, shots, shots on target and tackles with negative binomial models, recency half-lives, shrinkage, a game-state effect for corners and a referee factor for fouls. Why: Team and match markets, and the share given to each player. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Log score and over/under Brier per stat, settings chosen on 2024-25 and confirmed on 2025-26, model vs league-average baseline (blocks 15.4b-e).
Result: Kept corners 180 days, fouls 180 days with referee factor, yellows 365, reds 730, shots 90, shots on target 180, tackles 180. Reds referee factor removed (no gain).
Decision / where it lives: Kept

What changed: player_markets.py prices to score (1+, 2+, 3+), assist, goal or assist, shots and shots on target for every player and fixture, scaled to the match model's expected goals and the opponent, with assists per goal taken per run. Why: Player prop markets priced from the team model. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Brier (lower = better) for every market and line, out-of-sample on 2024-25 and 2025-26, model vs baseline, plus calibration of to score (blocks 15.5c-d).
Result: To score 0.0723 / 0.0684, assist 0.0596 / 0.0703, all beating baseline. Predicted vs actual scoring rate 8.6% vs 8.7% and 8.2% vs 8.0%.

What changed: Added fouls, fouled, tackles, to be carded, red card and keeper saves (1-5), with a per-market calibration (spread, level and shrink) kept only if it improved 2025-26. Why: Chances were too extreme before calibration (e.g. carded 0-10% band predicted 5.9% vs actual 8.6%). Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Same Brier test as 15.5 for the new markets; calibration fitted on 2024-25 and kept only if it improved 2025-26 (blocks 15.6b-c).
Result: Tackles 1+ 0.2059 / 0.2002, fouls 1+ 0.2210 / 0.2229, carded 0.1167 / 0.1101, saves 3+ 0.2346 / 0.2428, all beating baseline. Carded bands after calibration 6.8 vs 8.0, 14.8 vs 14.1, 22.2 vs 22.4.
Decision / where it lives: Kept, calibration on for every market

What changed: Tested recency half-lives for every rate and a penalty-taker split (0.76 xG per penalty, FPL penalty order for upcoming games). Why: Bookmakers and analysts weight recent form and penalty duties. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Each recency half-life and the penalty split tested on to score and the other rates, chosen on 2024-25 and kept only if better on 2025-26 too.
Result: Penalty takers improved to score Brier 0.0707 to 0.0706 and 0.0673 to 0.0672. Recency no gain for goals; kept for xA (365 days), tackles (365) and reds (180).
Decision / where it lives: Kept (penalties on, selected half-lives)

What changed: match_markets.py prices team and match corners, fouls, cards, booking points, red card, most corners and most cards for every fixture; v_referee_forecast shows each referee's effect. Why: Match-level bet markets and referee-driven card and foul markets. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Brier over every line, model vs league-average baseline, both seasons, plus calibration of match cards and the referee forecasts tested (blocks 15.7b-f).
Result: Model vs baseline (2024-25 / 2025-26): fouls 0.1673 vs 0.1843 / 0.1711 vs 0.1783; cards 0.1537 vs 0.1574 / 0.1450 vs 0.1471; booking points 0.1581 vs 0.1620 / 0.1501 vs 0.1525; most corners 0.1673 vs 0.1901 / 0.1851 vs 0.1937; most cards 0.2134 vs 0.2195 / 0.2140 vs 0.2186. Match corners and red card tie.
Decision / where it lives: Kept; corners and red flagged "no better than league average"

What changed: slip_checker.py simulates each fixture 20,000 times so linked legs in one match are priced together, with fair odds and edge against a site's price. Why: Multiplying single chances misprices linked legs. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Three standard bet builders on every fixture of 2024-25 and 2025-26: actual hit rate vs simulated joint chance vs single chances multiplied (blocks 15.8a-b).
Result: Win + scorer: actual 20.8% vs simulated 21.8% vs product 15.7% (2024-25); 18.5% vs 18.7% vs 12.8% (2025-26). Scorer + 2 shots on target: 20.2 vs 18.2 vs 9.4; 15.1 vs 14.0 vs 6.3. Limit: cards and fouls simulated separately. Fixed 16 Oct 2026 to work on upcoming games.
Decision / where it lives: Kept

What changed: v_market_tests gathers every market, line and season with predicted vs actual chance and model vs baseline Brier. Why: One place to show what is shown on the dashboard and why. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Every market-line counted as beats / ties / loses to baseline, per season (v_market_tests, blocks 15.9b-c).
Result: 117 of 126 market-lines beat baseline in 2024-25 and 110 of 126 in 2025-26; the rest are red cards, match corners and extreme lines.
Decision / where it lives: Rule set: a market is shown if it beats baseline over all its lines in both seasons

What changed: New dashboard sheets from v_player_markets_next, v_match_markets_next, v_referee_forecast, v_player_vs_opponent, v_market_calibration and v_player_list, plus the Slip sheet from slip_results. What changed: calibrate.py: calibration slope for home, draw and away, then a sharpening power (chance^a, renormalised) fitted on one season and tested on the other. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26, each match predicted once by the latest run before it (350 per season); RPS and log loss vs bookmakers on the same matches.
Result: Slopes 1.3-1.5 for home/away (+/-0.22); fitted powers disagree (1.089 and 0.977); RPS changed +/-0.0002 and log loss worse in both seasons. Model 0.2077 / 0.2023 vs bookmakers 0.2041 / 0.2008.
Decision / where it lives: NOT ADOPTED. CAL_POWER = 1.0. The model is calibrated; the gap to the bookmakers is information, not scaling.

What changed: market_blend.py: proportional, power and Shin margin removal on closing odds; model weight against Bet365 fitted by log loss (1X2 and over/under 2.5 separately); VALUE flag replayed and judged by the closing line. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Margins 2023-24 to 2025-26; weights 2024-25 and 2025-26 (350 matches each); VALUE replay at weights 0-0.5: expected ROI = Bet365 price x closing fair chance - 1.
Result: Margin methods within 0.002 (power best). Model weight 0.25 for 1X2 (0.34 / 0.14 by season), 0.00 for over/under. VALUE flags lost about 6-12% against the close at every weight (t-stat -3.6 to -15).
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED: power margin, weights 0.25 / 0.0, source ens_dcxg_50. No betting edge on 1X2 or goals.

What changed: weekly.py stores each price's closing fair chance; v_value_log adds exp_roi_close_pct and kelly_stake_pct, v_value_summary adds exp_roi_close_pct, t_stat and verdict. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Built into the weekly run; verdict after 100+ settled prices (t-stat beyond +/-2).
Result: Pending: too few settled prices.
Decision / where it lives: ADOPTED. Quarter Kelly, 1% cap.

What changed: significance.py: paired bootstrap by match (5,000 redraws) of the RPS change for every upgrade, per season, plus log loss. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26 runs after GW3 to GW34, 700 matches, predictions both models made.
Result: Only the ratings blend is a proven gain: -0.0126 (95% interval -0.0174 to -0.0076). All later upgrades within +/-0.002 and not individually significant. Gap to bookmakers 0.0071 (0.0022 to 0.0120). Full table: upgrade_significance.csv.
Decision / where it lives: Kept ens_dcxg_50. Next gains need new information (line-ups, team news).

What changed: scoreline_check.py: predicted vs actual counts of each scoreline, draws, big wins and total goals; best Dixon-Coles low-score correction. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: 700 matches, main model's expected goals from the run just before each match; z-scores and chi-square.
Result: 1-0 over-predicted (45 vs 66, z -2.7), 2-2 under-predicted (57 vs 36, z +3.6), both teams score z +2.0; total goals p = 0.066; best rho -0.08 (log loss -0.0018 per match).
Decision / where it lives: NOT ADOPTED (no effect on markets in use). Correlated goals noted for correct score / both teams to score.

What changed: prop_audit.py: player totals vs football-data team totals (Part A) and vs an Opta sample from FotMob (Part B). Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Part A: 830 matches. Part B: 20 matches of 2026-27 GW6-7, 607 players matched.
Result: Part A ratios: fouls 1.00, fouled 1.03-1.04 (expected), shots 1.00-1.03, SOT 1.00. Part B (Opta / yours): fouls 0.996, fouled 1.000, shots 1.000, SOT 1.000; 100% identical per player. Found 2026-27 player data leaving blanks for zeros (1,125 rows).
Decision / where it lives: No scaling needed. Blank-for-zero fixed in player_data.py and the database.

Result: Pending.

What changed: xi_test.py: the main model's expected goals adjusted by attack and selection factors from the actual starting XIs vs the expected XIs (player_rates backtest), fitted on one season and tested on the other. Why: tests whether line-up information is where the bookmakers' edge comes from. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: 2024-25 and 2025-26, 700 matches; bootstrap 95% interval by match.
Result: RPS change +0.0002 (95% interval -0.0022 to +0.0027); slightly worse in both seasons; closed none of the gap to the bookmakers.
Decision / where it lives: FAIL. Expected-XI model (old Upgrade 31) dropped. Next suspect: stale ratings (runs every 3-5 gameweeks).

What changed: season_tails.py: PIT, 50/80/95% coverage and tail bands for every run's finishing-position chances. Date: Oct 2026.
How it was tested: Excel sims (one season) and Python dyn sims (two seasons), by stage of the season.
Result: dyn_10 honest at every stage (80% coverage 82-92%). Excel sims overconfident in GW1-10: 48% inside the 80% range, PIT end bins 65% (p = 0.003); fine from GW23.
Decision / where it lives: Quote the dyn_10 chances up to GW10; Excel season sim to be replaced in Python.

What changed: leak_check.py: 8 automatic tests that no forecast used information from after kick-off (frozen ratings or sims, late availability, late runs, rescheduled games, xG for unplayed games, value and prop logs). Date: Oct 2026.

Result: All clear apart from one rescheduled 2024-25 game (harmless) and a pre-season run loaded late (not a leak; test now skips pre-season runs).
Decision / where it lives: Run after every weekly run.
